s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent lateral knee pain with an intra-articular space-occupying lesion
salient_findings: Recurrent pain localized to the lateral side of the left knee
Intra-articular space-occupying lesion invading the tibial plateau on MRI
Lesion with heterogeneous appearance on T2-weighted images and peripheral rim enhancement on gadolinium-enhanced MRI
key_facts: 30-year-old Asian man
6-month history of recurrent pain
Pain localized to the lateral side of the left knee
Slight tenderness and swelling over the lateral joint line
Plain radiographs were unremarkable
Routine laboratory tests were within normal limits
MRI demonstrated a 1.5 cm intra-articular space-occupying lesion
Lesion invaded the tibial plateau
Lesion was homogeneous and isointense to muscle on T1-weighted images
Lesion appeared heterogeneous with internal specks on T2-weighted images
No satellite lesions identified on gadolinium-enhanced MRI

shortlist.label: Giant cell tumor of bone
shortlist.why_kept: Intra-articular space-occupying lesion with characteristic MRI findings

shortlist.label: Chondroblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Lesion location and MRI appearance consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Chondromyxoid fibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Rare tumor that can present with similar clinical and imaging features

shortlist.label: Pigmented villonodular synovitis
shortlist.why_kept: Intra-articular lesion with heterogeneous appearance on MRI

shortlist.label: Synovial chondromatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Multiple intra-articular lesions possible, but single lesion also reported

shortlist.label: Chondrosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Malignant tumor that can present with similar imaging characteristics

shortlist.label: Osteoid osteoma
shortlist.why_kept: Small, benign tumor that can cause recurrent pain

shortlist.label: Synovial sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Malignant tumor that can present with similar clinical and imaging features

raw.rationale: The lesion's location in the epiphysis or apophysis, particularly in the tibial plateau, and its appearance on MRI with a heterogeneous signal and internal specks on T2-weighted images, along with peripheral rim enhancement on gadolinium-enhanced sequences, are characteristic of chondroblastoma.

rejected.label: Giant cell tumor of bone
rejected.why: Typically occurs in skeletally mature individuals and has a more aggressive appearance on imaging

rejected.label: Chondromyxoid fibroma
rejected.why: Less common and usually has a more lobulated appearance on imaging

rejected.label: Pigmented villonodular synovitis
rejected.why: Typically involves the entire synovial lining and has a more diffuse pattern on imaging

rejected.label: Synovial chondromatosis
rejected.why: Characterized by multiple small cartilaginous nodules within the synovium, not a single large lesion

rejected.label: Chondrosarcoma
rejected.why: Usually occurs in older adults and has a more aggressive appearance on imaging with cortical destruction and soft tissue extension

rejected.label: Osteoid osteoma
rejected.why: Typically presents with a small nidus and surrounding sclerosis, not a large intra-articular lesion

rejected.label: Synovial sarcoma
rejected.why: Usually occurs near the joints but not within them and has a more aggressive appearance on imaging
